annotations.text:
PLACEHOLDER IMAGERY

All 16 images are public-domain works from the Art Institute of Chicago — Homer, Sargent, Le Gray, Watkins — standing in for Zenon's work.

Titles, dates and dimensions are the real ones, which is why they read 1856—1914. Swap in real work and the captions keep their shape.

Anything in [SQUARE BRACKETS] is copy I drafted or left for you to fill.

WHY THE TWO ROOMS LOOK DIFFERENT

The colour came out of the work rather than a guess. The watercolours cluster cool — teal, hue 150-200. The photographs cluster warm — sepia, hue 40-50. So paper-cream sets off the paintings, warm charcoal sets off the prints.

Identical in both: wordmark, nav, caption grammar, 1px rules, vertical rhythm.

Different: the ground, and 3-up matted versus 2-up large.

WHAT THIS PULLS FROM YOUR SCHEMA

The caption line uses four fields the site renders nowhere today: medium, yearCreated, dimensions, price. ArtworkCard currently shows title and year only.

Two gaps I ran into: there is no support field, so captions say "Watercolour" rather than "Watercolour on paper"; and no availability field, so a sold work can only fall back to "Enquire".

The rooms key off medium, so the "acrylic on canvas" TODO adds a third room instead of forcing a redesign.

ON THE HOMEPAGE TODO

notes.md has "remove duplicate name display on homepage" open.

So the name appears exactly once, in the header. The hero leads with the tagline instead of repeating it — which is why the big line is "Two ways of looking at landscape" and not the artist's name.

TWO OTHER STANCES

Sketches rather than finished pages — enough to point at.

B lists the work as an archive, with medium as a column instead of a room. C shows one piece at a time on a single dark ground and drops the room split altogether.

Each artboard carries its own tradeoff at the bottom.
